  всплывало загадочным несовпадением шифротекста), `BLEResponseParserTests` (каждая документированная строка →
  свой типизированный случай), `BLEPinSessionTests` (**локаут переживает `invalidateOnDisconnect()`, сессия — нет**),
  `WiFiNetworkStatusTests`, `BLECommandTests` (регистр аргументов выживает), `RobotSessionCompatibilityGateTests`.
- `BLECommandPumpTests` поверх `FakeBLETransport`: главный регрессионный тест — **синхронная команда возвращает
  прочитанное значение, ни разу не ожидая нотификации** (ловушка №1); ack пропускается только если прочитано

  запроса `connect_sealed`; 404 → `.wirelessFeaturesUnavailable`.

  `"ghi\njkl"` → `abc`, `defghi`, `jkl`; гейт сброса не открывается, пока не выполнены все три условия).

**Вектор для sealing.** `cryptography` в `.venv-sim` нет, и трогать `Scripts/sim-requirements.txt` нельзя —
его sha256 привязан к базовой версии демона и заставил бы всех пересобирать венв MuJoCo. Поэтому отдельный
`Scripts/seal-fixture-requirements.txt` и ручной (никогда не в CI) `Scripts/generate-seal-fixture.py`:
фиксированные ключи и nonce, `ssid` с пробелом (ловит кодировку AAD), `pin` в смешанном регистре (ловит регистр
соли), самопроверка обратной расшифровкой перед печатью, результат в
`Tests/ReachyKitTests/Fixtures/wifi_seal_vector.json` (таргет уже объявляет `.copy("Fixtures")`).

находит, по `…cdef0` — нет; запроса pairing нет; `PING` приходит **чтением, без нотификации**; порядок

вернул скан; `JOURNAL_READ` выше ~182 байт; сквозной sealing с верным и неверным паролем (возврат в
`reachy-mini-ap` за ~60 с); протухший `kid` после 600 с и восстановление одним повторным KEYEX;
`…cdef7` == `/api/daemon/hardware-id`; `CMD_RESTART_DAEMON` (ответа нет, ошибка записи, нужен повторный PIN);
`CMD_HOTSPOT` и `CMD_WIFI_RESET` — **до** software reset, это путь отхода; реальное обновление робота на релиз
назад (10–20 мин); `pre_release=true` даёт другую версию; `available_version == "unknown"` воспроизводится
блокировкой WAN робота; `CMD_SOFTWARE_RESET` — **последним и один раз**, убедившись что `/restore/venvs` на месте.

**Насовсем.** `POST /wifi/connect?ssid=&password=` (PSK в query string — только `connect_sealed`, везде);
`/update/start-from-ref` и `/validate-ref` (произвольные git-ref; апстрим намеренно не отдаёт их по BLE);
`WIFI_FORGET`/`forget_all` **из BLE-консоли** (забыть сеть, которая вот-вот понадобится — грабли; оставить в
LAN-настройках); `NEHotspotConfiguration` для автовхода в `reachy-mini-ap` (требует entitlement, правки профиля
и объяснений на ревью ради экономии одного похода в Настройки); `UIBackgroundModes` и state restoration; парсинг

(`ECHO:` — всё, чего добьётся неизвестная команда).

**Если срез затянется.** Экран `SET_NAME` в онбординге и карточка Wi-Fi в настройках (шаг 21).

Тесты упали — и это ценно: мой новый набор вскрыл латентную гонку в тестовой оснастке.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
`StubURLProtocol` хранит таблицу заглушек в **глобальной статике** (`private nonisolated(unsafe) static var stubs`). Внутри одного `@Suite(.serialized)` это безопасно, но `swift test --parallel` гоняет **разные сюиты одновременно**, и они затирают таблицу друг у друга. `RobotConnectionStatusMappingTests` жил с этим спокойно ровно потому, что был единственным пользователем — мой второй набор превратил латентную гонку в стабильное падение трёх тестов.

Это ровно тот класс проблем, про который предупреждает правило 7 («тесты ждут условий, а не длительностей»): оснастка с общим глобальным состоянием даёт зелёный результат по чистой удаче. Чиню как часть шага A2, который и так был про `StubURLProtocol`.

test(kit): bind stub responses to the session that carries them

`swift test --parallel` runs separate suites concurrently, so the shared static
stub table let one suite answer another suite's requests, or wipe them
mid-flight. `.serialized` was no defence — it orders tests within one suite and
says nothing about the others. A second suite reaching for the harness turned
that latent race into three deterministic failures.

Route keys now also accept a query, so `?pre_release=true` and `?pre_release=false`
stop collapsing onto a single stub.
EOF

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(kit): read the hardware id as the daemon reports it

`/api/daemon/hardware-id` answers with one key, `{"hardware_id": "<16 hex>"}` —
`sha256(usb serial)[:16]`. The handshake was flattening that map into
`"hardware_id=<value>"`; the comment calling the entries "component serials" was
stale.

The value is a join key, not a display string: the robot hands out the same
string over BLE and advertises it as the mDNS `unit_id`, so recognising a
just-provisioned robot on the LAN is a plain `==`. Reshaping it broke that
silently — nothing threw, the match simply never happened.

The status payload already carries the field, so the common path now costs one
request fewer; the dedicated route stays as the fallback for daemons that omit it.
EOF
git log --oneline -3 && git status --porcelain && echo "(clean)"

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(kit): add the daemon self-update client

`/update/*` is hand-written for three reasons the generated client cannot work
around: it sits at the app root rather than under `/api`, it is mounted only when
the daemon runs with `--wireless-version`, and the committed `openapi.json` is
generated without that flag, so the spec has never seen it.

It gets its own protocol rather than joining `RobotAPIClient`, which describes the
surface `RobotSession` needs to connect. Keeping them apart also spares every
existing test double three more methods to stub.

Two daemon answers are easy to misreport and are modelled explicitly. An
`available_version` of `"unknown"` means the robot could not reach PyPI — the
robot's connectivity is at fault, not the request. And a Lite robot's 404 on a
route it never mounts is a capability answer, not a missing resource, so only
`/update/info` keeps its literal 404.
EOF

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(kit): stream update job logs

`ws://…/update/ws/logs?job_id=…` differs from the daemon journal in two ways that
both look like working streams when handled wrongly.

It carries two frame shapes at once: `bg_job_register.ws_poll_info` sends every new
line as its own text frame and *then* a `JobInfo` JSON frame repeating those same
lines. Decoding both duplicates the whole log, so a frame that parses as JSON
contributes only its status.

And it never reconnects. The job finishes by restarting the daemon, which kills the
process — and the in-memory job register with it — before the terminal `done` frame
is written. The socket closing is what completion looks like; reconnecting would
hammer a rebooting daemon and could never find the job again.

The harness gains a send completion so a test that closes the connection straight
after a frame stops racing the frame it is asserting on.
EOF
git log --oneline -2

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(kit): offer a daemon update instead of failing the connection

An unsupported daemon threw out of the handshake, which surfaced as a generic
connect failure and a "Try again" button that could never work — the version was
not going to change by retrying. The robot's own `/update/*` route is the way out
of that state, so the handshake now reports the verdict and the session halts on a
new `needsDaemonUpdate` step, latched even for automatic attempts so the 10 s
rescan stops hammering the robot. `canSelfUpdate` carries `wireless_version`,
because a Lite robot never mounts `/update/*` and needs the desktop app over USB.

ADR 0001 is unchanged in substance and now enforced in code rather than by
layout: `assertSupportedDaemon()` guards wake, sleep and every call routed through
`withClient`, so an unsupported daemon is refused even if some future screen
reaches past the connection gate.

The stepper gains a compatibility row. Spelling out the new step in the outcome
table pushed it past the complexity limit and exposed that it was one rule written
eleven times — a step stands on a stage, everything before it is done, everything
after is pending. The unchanged `RobotSessionStageOutcomeTests` pins the result.
EOF

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(ui): let the user update a robot the app cannot talk to

Replaces the dead end a too-old daemon used to land on. The screen states both
versions, checks what the robot can reach, streams the installer output into the
extracted log console, and waits out the restart.

Two states exist because the daemon reports them and they need different words
from a generic failure. A robot that cannot reach PyPI is offline — its own
connectivity is the problem. A Lite robot never mounts `/update/*` at all, so it
gets an explanation and no button, since nothing the app does could work.

Success is inferred, not observed: the update ends by restarting the daemon, so
the app reconnects and compares versions. Coming back on the old version is a
failure worth naming — it means a new enough release is not published yet, which
looks nothing like "the update crashed".
EOF

1	# ADR 0001: Daemon compatibility and LAN security
2	
3	- Status: Accepted
4	- Date: 2026-08-03
5	
6	## Context
7	
8	The daemon updates independently, its OpenAPI document has no stability guarantee, and its hand-written WebSockets
9	are outside that document. Daemon 1.9.0 is the version verified against the simulator and recorded state fixture.
10	The daemon exposes motion commands over plaintext HTTP/WebSocket and has no authentication API.
11	
12	## Decision: compatibility
13	
14	- Daemon 1.9.0 is both the minimum supported and tested baseline for this client.
15	- Handshake reads status/version before identity or any robot command.
16	- A parseable 1.x version below 1.9.0, or any different major version, is rejected with an actionable error.
17	- A newer 1.x version is allowed with a persistent compatibility warning. Unknown JSON fields remain tolerated.
18	- A missing or malformed version is allowed in limited/unknown mode with a warning, because older deployments may
19	  omit metadata even when their endpoint shape works.
20	- Optional endpoint failure disables that feature; it must not invalidate an otherwise healthy session.
21	- `Scripts/sim-requirements.txt` pins the simulator baseline. Updating it requires updating the policy, fixture and
22	  compatibility tests together after a live simulator check.
23	
24	## Decision: security
25	
26	Version 1 supports only a trusted private LAN or the robot's own access point. The UI states that transport is
27	unauthenticated and unencrypted. Users must not expose port 8000 through port forwarding, a public IP, or an
28	untrusted network. Client-side tokens or a fake pairing screen are explicitly rejected: without daemon support they
29	provide no security.
30	
31	Authenticated remote access is a release blocker, not a client-only follow-up. It requires an upstream daemon
32	protocol for pairing, authenticated HTTP/WebSocket requests and transport encryption. Credentials must then live in
33	Keychain and be injected centrally by ReachyKit.
34	
35	## Consequences
36	
37	Anyone with network access to the daemon can command the robot. Server-side motion limits remain the safety boundary.
38	The compatibility warning is informative for newer/unknown daemons; unsupported versions fail before commands.
39

input.new_string:
## Decision: recovering from an unsupported daemon

Amendment, 2026-08-04. Rejecting an unsupported version by throwing out of the handshake left the user on a "Try
again" button that could never work — the version does not change by retrying. Rejection is kept; the dead end is not.

- The handshake reports the verdict instead of throwing. The session halts on a dedicated `needsDaemonUpdate` step,
  latched even for automatic attempts so the periodic rescan stops re-probing a robot it has already identified.
- **No command reaches an unsupported daemon.** This is enforced in code, not by navigation: `assertSupportedDaemon()`
  guards wake, sleep and every call routed through `withClient`. Keeping the control screens unmounted is a layout
  decision and does not count as enforcement.
- The routes that stay open are `GET /api/daemon/{status,hardware-id,robot-name}` and `/update/*`. These are reads and
  version negotiation, not the command surface, and `/update/*` is the only route that can end the condition.
- `/update/*` is mounted only under `--wireless-version`. A Lite robot cannot self-update, so it is told to use the
  official desktop app over USB rather than offered a button that must fail.
- Success is inferred by reconnecting and comparing versions. The update ends with `systemctl restart`, which kills
  the daemon before it can report a terminal job status, so neither the log socket nor `/update/info` can confirm it.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate the known-answer vector for `WiFiPasswordSeal`.

Run by hand, never in CI — it exists so the Swift test can assert a *reproducible*
ciphertext against an implementation of the scheme that is not our own. The daemon
side is `daemon/app/routers/wifi_config.py` (`get_provisioning_key`,
`_open_sealed_psk`) in pollen-robotics/reachy_mini.

    python3 -m venv /tmp/seal && /tmp/seal/bin/pip install -q -r Scripts/seal-fixture-requirements.txt
    /tmp/seal/bin/python Scripts/generate-seal-fixture.py > Tests/ReachyKitTests/Fixtures/wifi_seal_vector.json

Keys and nonce are fixed so the output is stable. The SSID carries a space and the
PIN mixes case: both are fed into the key derivation (as AAD and as HKDF salt), so a
client that normalises either would still pass a test using plain ASCII.
"""

import base64
import json
import sys

from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import hashes
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.x25519 import X25519PrivateKey
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.kdf.hkdf import HKDF

INFO = b"reachy-mini-wifi-psk-v1"

ROBOT_PRIVATE = bytes(range(32))
CLIENT_PRIVATE = bytes(range(32, 64))
NONCE = bytes(range(0x10, 0x1C))  # 12 bytes

SSID = "Reachy Test Net"
REDACTED = "REDACTED"
PIN = "4A7f9"
KID = "0a1b2c3d"


def derive(shared: bytes) -> bytes:
    return HKDF(algorithm=hashes.SHA256(), length=32, salt=PIN.encode(), info=INFO).derive(shared)


def main() -> None:
    robot_private = X25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(ROBOT_PRIVATE)
    robot_public = robot_private.public_key()
    client_private = X25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(CLIENT_PRIVATE)

    key = derive(client_private.exchange(robot_public))
    ciphertext = AESGCM(key).encrypt(NONCE, REDACTED.encode(), SSID.encode())

    # Reproduce what the daemon does on receipt. A vector that cannot be opened by
    # the other side is worse than no vector at all, so never emit one.
    reopened = AESGCM(derive(robot_private.exchange(client_private.public_key()))).decrypt(
        NONCE, ciphertext, SSID.encode()
    )
    if reopened.decode() != REDACTED:
        sys.exit("round trip failed: the daemon side would not open this ciphertext")

    def b64(raw: bytes) -> str:
        return base64.b64encode(raw).decode()

    json.dump(
        {
            "ssid": SSID,
            "password": REDACTED,
            "pin": PIN,
            "kid": KID,
            "robotPublicKey": b64(robot_public.public_bytes_raw()),
            "clientPrivateKey": b64(CLIENT_PRIVATE),
            "nonce": b64(NONCE),
            "expectedClientPublicKey": b64(client_private.public_key().public_bytes_raw()),
            "expectedCiphertext": b64(ciphertext),
        },
        sys.stdout,
        indent=2,
    )
    sys.stdout.write("\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(kit): seal Wi-Fi passwords for provisioning

Implements the daemon's `x25519-hkdf-sha256-aesgcm` scheme, which is why BLE
provisioning is possible at all: the Wi-Fi password never crosses Bluetooth in the
clear, a hard requirement for App Store review and the reason upstream built this
route for a mobile client in the first place.

The derivation has no feedback loop. Drift by one byte in the salt, the info label
or the AAD and the robot answers `ERROR: Bad credentials (wrong PIN?)`, which is
indistinguishable from the user mistyping the PIN. So it is pinned against a
known-answer vector generated by the daemon's own Python library, with fixed keys
and nonce; the generator refuses to emit a vector the daemon side cannot reopen.
An RFC 5869 case sits beside it so a change in CryptoKit's HKDF names itself
instead of surfacing as an unexplained ciphertext mismatch.

The vector's SSID carries a space and its PIN mixes case, since both feed the key
derivation — a client that normalised either would still pass on plain ASCII.

The generator has its own requirements file: `sim-requirements.txt` is checksummed
against the daemon baseline and touching it forces a full MuJoCo venv rebuild.

Upstream's documented limitation is carried over verbatim rather than papered
over: this defeats a passive listener, not an active man-in-the-middle within
Bluetooth range during setup, who could brute-force the five-character PIN offline.
EOF
git log --oneline -1

feat(kit): drive BLE commands one at a time

The pump exists because the robot answers on two different channels and upstream's
own `BLE_WIFI_PROVISIONING.md` documents only one of them. It claims every command
notifies; `CommandCharacteristic.WriteValue` in fact assigns the response value
directly and never calls `send_notification`, so `PING`, `STATUS`, `PIN_…` and the
journal commands answer on a *read*. Only daemon-proxied commands go through
`_emit_response`, acknowledging with `OK: working` and delivering the real result
later.

So: write, read, and await a notification only if the read was the ack. Following
the documentation instead would hang forever on the very first `PING`.

Two more properties fall out of the robot's implementation. It sets the response
value before checking whether anyone subscribed, so a lost notification is
recovered by re-reading rather than by failing. And with one response
characteristic and no correlation id, concurrent commands would race for the same
reply — actors are reentrant, so the serialisation is built explicitly.

An oversized payload is refused rather than fragmented: the robot's handler
ignores write offsets, so a split `WIFI_CONNECT_ENC` would be dispatched as two
unrecognised commands. Whether the real payload fits at all is the first thing to
check on hardware.
EOF

## Что сделано и лежит в ветке `feat/ble-wifi-provisioning`

13 коммитов, 272 теста зелёные, линтер и форматирование чистые, целевое приложение собирается.

**Блок A — фундамент.** Починен hardware id: `handshake()` схлопывал `{"hardware_id": "<16 hex>"}` в строку `"hardware_id=abc…"`, из-за чего связка «робот, настроенный по BLE» ↔ «робот, появившийся в сети» не сработала бы никогда. Заодно `StubURLProtocol` перестал держать заглушки в глобальной статике — мой второй набор тестов превратил латентную гонку между параллельными сюитами в стабильное падение. `LogConsoleView` вынесен из экрана и больше не знает о транспорте.

**Блок B — гейт обновления.** Тупик «Try again», который не мог сработать, заменён на рабочий путь: клиенты `/update/*`, WebSocket лога задания, фаза `needsDaemonUpdate` и экран обновления с тумблером беты. ADR 0001 дополнен.

**Блок C — настройки.** Отдельный экран вместо трёх разрозненных мест, переименование робота, карточка обновления.

**Блок D — ядро BLE, частично.** Все чистые типы протокола, криптография запечатывания пароля с контрольным вектором, шов транспорта, помпа команд, `NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription`.

## Чего нет

Три вещи из блока D и целиком блоки E и F:

- **`CoreBluetoothTransport`** — реальный адаптер. Протокол `BLETransport` и фейк для тестов есть, живого CoreBluetooth нет, поэтому **на роботе проверить пока нечего**.
- **`BLEProvisioningSession`** — оркестровка поверх помпы.
- **`/wifi/*` по HTTP** — перенёс из блока B в D (объяснял почему: его протокол-родитель определяется вместе с криптографией).
- **Онбординг** (блок E) и **BLE-консоль восстановления** (блок F) — не начаты.

Задача №4 в списке обновлена: там записано ровно то, что осталось, с деталями. Блоки B и C при этом самодостаточны — экран обновления демона можно проверять на живом роботе прямо сейчас.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
Две находки, которые стоили бы отладки на железе, если бы всплыли позже. **Документация апстрима про BLE неверна**: она утверждает, что все команды отвечают нотификацией, но `WriteValue` присваивает значение напрямую — клиент, написанный «по докам», зависал бы на первом же `PING`. И **`WIFI_CONNECT_ENC` (~260 байт) не влезает в дефолтный ATT MTU iOS (185)**, а обработчик робота игнорирует смещения записи. Поэтому шаг 0 верификации — измерить `maximumWriteValueLength` на живом роботе **до** того, как что-то строится сверху; если фрагментация подтвердится, запасной путь через HTTP по хотспоту становится обязательным, и `WiFiProvisioningTransport` в плане существует именно ради этого.

content.text:
Закоммичено — [e56acd3](.githooks/pre-push), рабочее дерево чистое.

Поправка к тому, что я сказал раньше: это **не артефакты `hk`**, а хуки Git LFS — их пишет `git lfs install` в тот каталог, на который указывает `core.hooksPath`. Отсюда и то, что они появлялись сами по себе.

Стоит знать про цену: каждый хук делает `command -v git-lfs || exit 2`, и в случае `pre-push` это **блокирует пуш целиком** у любого, у кого git-lfs не установлен. При этом репозиторий сейчас в LFS ничего не хранит — ни `.gitattributes`, ни единого LFS-файла (`git lfs ls-files` пуст). То есть коммит делает git-lfs обязательным для контрибьюторов и CI, ничего пока не давая взамен. Записал это в тело коммита.

Если LFS в планах нет, разумнее было бы `git lfs uninstall --local` и `.gitignore` на эти четыре файла — но это твоё решение, и откатить один коммит на ветке тривиально.

Итого в ветке `feat/ble-wifi-provisioning` 14 коммитов. Остаток работы (CoreBluetooth-адаптер, `BLEProvisioningSession`, `/wifi/*`, онбординг, консоль восстановления) записан в задаче №4 с деталями.

2. **Safety lives in the daemon.** All robot commands go through the daemon API. Never duplicate or bypass motion

6. **Conventional commits** — enforced by the commit-msg hook. The pre-commit hook stages _every_ modified `*.swift`
   and `*.md` (`stage` in `hk.pkl`), not only what you `git add` — separate unrelated edits with
   `git stash push <paths>` first, or they land in one commit.
7. **Tests wait on conditions, not durations.** A fixed `Task.sleep` before an assertion is a CI flake waiting to
   happen: the suites are `@MainActor` and a loaded runner starves them. Poll the condition, and give an injected

`CLAUDE.md` — симлинк на `AGENTS.md`, правки пойдут в реальные файлы. Вот что предлагаю добавить.

---

### Update: `./AGENTS.md` (Quick Reference)

**Why:** симулятор нельзя заставить отдавать `/wifi/*` и `/update/*` — на это уйдёт время у любого, кто попробует.

```diff
+ `sim-daemon` **cannot** serve `/wifi/*` or `/update/*`: passing `--wireless-version` crashes on import
+ (`.venv-sim` has neither `nmcli` nor `cryptography`), and `main.py` would run robot-image maintenance on your Mac.
+ Those routes are covered by `StubURLProtocol` / `LocalWebSocketServer` and real hardware only. BLE likewise —
+ the robot's GATT service is Linux/BlueZ, so nothing simulates it.
```

**Why:** прямой вызов форматтера уходит в `Apps/DerivedData` на несколько ГБ сгенерированного кода.

```diff
- (`./bin/mise x -- swiftlint lint --strict Sources Tests Apps/ReachySpike`).
+ (`./bin/mise x -- swiftlint lint --strict Sources Tests Apps/ReachySpike`). Always pass those explicit paths —
+ a bare `.` walks into `Apps/DerivedData`, and swiftformat then "fails" on generated and vendored sources.
```

---

### Update: `./AGENTS.md` (Project Rules 6 и 7)

**Why:** правило 6 сейчас подразумевает, что хук стейджит всё; на не-Swift файлах коммит просто падает.

```diff
   `git stash push <paths>` first, or they land in one commit.
+  Only those two extensions: `.py`, `.json`, fixtures and hook scripts need an explicit `git add`, and a commit
+  with nothing staged fails before the hook runs.
```

**Why:** `swift test --parallel` гоняет сюиты одновременно — общее глобальное состояние в оснастке даёт зелёный результат по случайности.

```diff
   timeout headroom its deadline cannot cut short.
+  `--parallel` also runs *suites* concurrently and `.serialized` orders only within one — a harness holding shared
+  global state passes until a second suite uses it (`StubURLProtocol` binds stubs to their session for this reason).
+  Give async transport tests `.timeLimit(.minutes(1))`, or one hang stalls the whole run.
```

---

### Update: `.claude/rules/daemon-api.md`

**Why:** три факта, каждый из которых иначе всплывает как «клиент молча делает не то».

```diff
+ - **Wireless-only routes.** `/wifi/*` and `/update/*` mount at the app ROOT (no `/api`) and only under
+   `--wireless-version`. The committed spec is generated without that flag, so they are absent from it and the
+   generated client cannot reach them — hand-write them. A Lite robot 404s; gate on `DaemonStatus.wireless_version`.
+ - `/update/ws/logs` sends each line as a text frame AND then a `JobInfo` JSON frame repeating those same lines —
+   decode JSON first and ignore its `logs`, or every line doubles. The job ends with `systemctl restart`, which
+   kills the daemon before a terminal `done`: the socket closing is completion, confirmed by reconnecting and
+   comparing versions. `available_version: "unknown"` means the ROBOT could not reach PyPI.
+ - `GET /api/daemon/hardware-id` answers one key, `{"hardware_id": "<16 hex>"}` = `sha256(usb serial)[:16]` — the
+   same string as mDNS TXT `unit_id` and BLE characteristic `…cdef7`. It is a join key: never reshape it.
```

---

### Update: `.claude/rules/networking.md` (замена блока про BLE)

**Why:** апстримовая документация врёт про нотификации — клиент, написанный по ней, зависает на первом `PING`.

```diff
- - BLE Wi-Fi provisioning protocol is documented upstream:
-   `reachy_mini/src/reachy_mini/daemon/app/services/bluetooth/BLE_WIFI_PROVISIONING.md` (phase 2; maps to CryptoKit
-   X25519 + HKDF-SHA256 + AES-GCM).
+ - BLE Wi-Fi provisioning (daemon 1.9.0+). Upstream doc:
+   `.../services/bluetooth/BLE_WIFI_PROVISIONING.md`; the authority is `bluetooth_service.py` beside it.
+   **The doc is wrong about replies:** it claims every command notifies, but `CommandCharacteristic.WriteValue`
+   assigns the response value directly — only daemon-proxied commands notify, after an `OK: working` ack. Pump is
+   write → read → await a notification only if the read was that ack. Awaiting unconditionally hangs on `PING`.
+ - The robot advertises the **status** service `…cdef3`, not the command service `…cdef0`, under the local name
+   `ReachyMini` — identical on every unit, so robots are told apart only after connecting, by `…cdef7`.
+ - `WIFI_CONNECT_ENC` is ~260 B against iOS's default ATT MTU of 185, and the robot ignores write offsets. Measure
+   `maximumWriteValueLength(for: .withResponse)` on hardware before building anything on top of provisioning.
+ - `WIFI_SCAN` is truncated to 180 bytes (~8–15 SSIDs, no pagination) — manual SSID entry is mandatory, not a
+   fallback. The PIN session dies on disconnect; the wrong-PIN lockout survives it.
```

---

### Update: `./Sources/ReachyKit/AGENTS.md`

**Why:** каждый новый тестовый дублёр спотыкается об это на первой сборке.

```diff
+ - `RobotAPIClient` supplies throwing defaults for everything except `handshake`, `daemonStatus`, `wakeUp` and
+   `gotoSleep` — every test double must implement those four. `/wifi/*` and `/update/*` live on separate protocols
+   so doubles for the connection surface stay small.
```

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. **Primary Request and Intent:**

   This session continues Phase 2 work on a native Swift client for the Reachy Mini Wireless robot, following an approved plan at `/Users/aleksei/.claude/plans/frolicking-gliding-nygaard.md` (blocks A–F).

   - **Message 2** (after `/compact`): "Продолжить с CoreBluetooth-адаптера можно в новой сессии — план лежит в frolicking-gliding-nygaard.md." — interpreted as: resume Block D starting with the CoreBluetooth adapter. Compacting is what you do to keep working in the same session, so I continued rather than stopping.
   - **Message 3**: `/claude-md-management:revise-claude-md` — review the session for learnings and update the CLAUDE.md files.
   - **Message 4**: "Применяй все кроме этого [the format-before-lint documentation addition] … Это надо поправить в конфиге hk, сделать зависастоть, сначал форматер затем линтер" — apply the other two doc additions, but do NOT document the format-before-lint workaround; instead fix the root cause in `hk.pkl` by declaring a dependency so the formatter runs before the linter.
   - **Message 5**: "комит" — commit.

2. **Key Technical Concepts:**
   - Swift 6 strict concurrency, `@MainActor @Observable`, actors, `AsyncStream`, `CheckedContinuation`, `@unchecked Sendable` + `NSLock`
   - CoreBluetooth: `CBCentralManager`, `CBPeripheral`, `CBCharacteristic`, ATT MTU, GATT, Just-Works pairing
   - swift-testing (`@Suite`/`@Test`/`#expect`/`#require`/`Issue.record`/`.timeLimit`)
   - CryptoKit: `Curve25519.KeyAgreement`, HKDF-SHA256, AES-GCM (`x25519-hkdf-sha256-aesgcm`)
   - swift-openapi-generator over committed `openapi.json`; hand-written clients for routes outside the spec
   - `mise` task runner (`./bin/mise run <task>`), `hk` (git hooks + format/lint orchestration, Pkl config), swiftformat, swiftlint `--strict`, xcsift, Tuist, dprint, actionlint
   - Conventional commits (commit-msg hook); pre-commit hook auto-stages every modified `*.swift`/`*.md` only
   - Protocol-injection test seams; `StubURLProtocol` (canned HTTP), `LocalWebSocketServer`, `FakeBLETransport`

3. **Files and Code Sections:**

   - **`Sources/ReachyKit/BLE/BLETransport.swift`** (modified) — added a push channel the scan UI needs:
     ```swift
     /// Everything that changes without being asked for.
     func events() -> AsyncStream<BLETransportEvent>
     
     public enum BLETransportEvent: Equatable, Sendable {
         case availabilityChanged(BLEAvailability)
         case discoveredChanged([BLEPeripheralSnapshot])
         /// Also delivered when the radio is switched off, which drops the link without any
         /// disconnect being requested.
         case disconnected(reason: String?)
     }
     ```

   - **`Sources/ReachyKit/BLE/CoreBluetoothTransport.swift`** (new) — the real adapter. Nonisolated `final class ... @unchecked Sendable`, one serial queue, lock-guarded snapshot. Key parts:
     ```swift
     public final class CoreBluetoothTransport: NSObject, BLETransport, @unchecked Sendable {
         static let minimumWriteLength = 20
         struct Snapshot { var availability = .unknown; var discovered: [BLEPeripheralSnapshot] = []
                           var maximumWriteLength = CoreBluetoothTransport.minimumWriteLength }
         private let queue = DispatchQueue(label: "com.alexey1312.reachy.bluetooth")
         private let lock = NSLock()
         // internal (not private) because the delegate lives in the neighbouring file:
         var peripherals, connected, characteristics, undiscoveredServices,
             pendingWrites, pendingReads, pendingNotifies, notificationListeners
     ```
     The load-bearing correction:
     ```swift
     /// Deliberately not `.withResponse`, which answers 512 on every iPhone: that is the
     /// maximum *attribute* length, reachable only because CoreBluetooth silently splits
     /// a longer value into ATT prepare/execute writes. The robot's `WriteValue` ignores
     /// `options["offset"]`… `.withoutResponse` reports `ATT_MTU - 3`.
     static func singlePacketWriteLength(of peripheral: CBPeripheral) -> Int {
         max(peripheral.maximumWriteValueLength(for: .withoutResponse), minimumWriteLength)
     }
     ```
     Plus `awaitingReply(timeout:start:expire:)` (queue-serialized continuation + timeout), `merging(_:into:)` (deterministic RSSI-desc ordering), `availability(for: CBManagerState)`.

   - **`Sources/ReachyKit/BLE/CoreBluetoothTransport+Delegate.swift`** (new) — `CBCentralManagerDelegate` + `CBPeripheralDelegate`. Documents that a read and a notification are the same callback:
     ```swift
     /// **A read and a notification are the same callback.** CoreBluetooth gives no way
     /// to tell them apart, so a pending read claims the value and anything else is
     /// treated as pushed…
     public func peripheral(_: CBPeripheral, didUpdateValueFor characteristic: CBCharacteristic, error: (any Error)?) {
         if let pending = pendingReads.removeValue(forKey: characteristic.uuid) { … return }
         guard error == nil, let value = characteristic.value else { return }
         for listener in notificationListeners.values { listener.yield(value) }
     }
     ```
     Also filters RSSI 127 ("no reading") on discovery.

   - **`Sources/ReachyKit/WiFi/WiFiProvisioningTransport.swift`** (new) — transport-independent provisioning:
     ```swift
     public protocol WiFiProvisioningTransport: Sendable {
         func provisioningKey() async throws -> WiFiProvisioningKey
         func scanNetworks() async throws -> [String]
         func connectSealed(_ payload: SealedWiFiCredentials) async throws
         func wifiStatus() async throws -> WiFiStatus
     }
     public enum WiFiJoinOutcome: Equatable, Sendable {
         case joined(WiFiStatus)
         case gaveUp(last: WiFiStatus?)
     }
     ```
     `WiFiProvisioning.join(...)` retries exactly once via `deservesFreshKey(_:)` = `(error as? BLECommandError) == .badCredentials`. `awaitJoin(using:timeout:pollInterval:)` polls with `status.mode == .wlan` as the condition (not `hasJoined(ssid:)`, because BLE never reports which network). `WiFiScanResult.networks(in:)` tries JSON then salvages complete quoted names from a truncated array.

   - **`Sources/ReachyKit/BLE/BLEProvisioningTransport.swift`** (new) — BLE implementation; `wifiStatus()` delegates to `networkStatus().status`; reads the characteristic rather than sending `WIFI_STATUS`.

   - **`Sources/ReachyKit/BLE/BLEResponse.swift`** (modified) — added:
     ```swift
     public func value() throws -> String {
         switch self {
         case let .failure(error): throw error
         case let .echo(command): throw BLECommandError.other("The robot did not understand “\(command)”.")
         case .pong: return "PONG"
         case let .ok(text), let .payload(text): return text
         }
     }
     ```

   - **`Sources/ReachyKit/BLE/BLEProvisioningSession.swift`** (new) — `@MainActor @Observable`, parallel to `RobotSession`. State: `availability`, `discovered`, `phase`, `pin`, `hardwareID`, `networkStatus: WiFiStatus?`, `robotAddress: String?`, `networks`, `lastError`. Methods: `startScan()`, `stopScan()`, `connect(to:)`, `authenticate(_:)`, `refreshNetworks()`, `join(ssid:password:)`, `rename(to:)`, `disconnect()`, `stop()`. Key comment:
     ```swift
     /// Held because the PIN is the HKDF salt: the password cannot be sealed without it,
     /// and sealing happens several screens after it was typed. It lives here rather than
     /// in a view model so that it dies with the link it belongs to, and it is never
     /// written anywhere — ADR 0001 leaves stored credentials to a real pairing protocol.
     private var verifiedPIN: String?
     ```

   - **`Sources/ReachyKit/BLE/WiFiNetworkStatus.swift`** (modified) — added `var status: WiFiStatus` conversion mapping `.connected` → `.wlan`, `.offline` → `.disconnected`, `.error` → `nil` mode + error string.

   - **`Sources/ReachyKit/Model/WiFiStatus.swift`** (pre-existing, discovered mid-work) — the correct shared type; `Decodable`, handles `connected`/`connected_network` and `known`/`known_networks`, tolerates unknown modes, has `hasJoined(_:)` and `didFallBackToHotspot`.

   - **`Sources/ReachyKit/WiFi/WiFiConfigClient.swift`** (new) — `protocol WiFiConfigClient: WiFiProvisioningTransport` adding `forget(ssid:)`, `forgetAll()`, `lastWiFiError()`, `resetWiFiError()`.

   - **`Sources/ReachyKit/Transport/RobotConnection+Wireless.swift`** (modified) — plumbing made internal and generalized:
     ```swift
     func wirelessJSON<T: Decodable>(method:path:queryItems:body:canReport404:) async throws -> T
     /// - Parameter canReport404: whether this route can legitimately answer 404…
     @discardableResult
     func wirelessData(method:path:queryItems:body:canReport404:) async throws -> Data
     ```
     Replaced the hardcoded `path != "/update/info"` check; `updateInfo` now passes `canReport404: true`.

   - **`Sources/ReachyKit/Transport/RobotConnection+WiFi.swift`** (new) — `extension RobotConnection: WiFiConfigClient`. `scanNetworks()` is a POST to `/wifi/scan_and_list`. `connectSealed` maps 400 → `BLECommandError.badCredentials`, 409 → `.busy`. `forget` passes `canReport404: true`.

   - **`Tests/ReachyKitTests/Support/FakeBLETransport.swift`** (modified) — added `events()`, `emit(_:)`, `isObservingEvents`, and per-characteristic reads:
     ```swift
     var characteristicValues: [BLECharacteristicID: String] = [:]
     func read(_ characteristic: BLECharacteristicID) async throws -> Data {
         if characteristic != .response, let value = characteristicValues[characteristic] { return Data(value.utf8) }
         return Data(lock.withLock { lastRead }.utf8)
     }
     ```

   - **`Tests/ReachyKitTests/Support/FakeProvisioningTransport.swift`** (new) — real X25519 keys, `refusesFirst`, `scanReply`, `connectsAfterReads`.

   - **`Tests/ReachyKitTests/Support/StubURLProtocol.swift`** (modified) — added request recording so a test can prove the PSK never reaches a URL:
     ```swift
     static func requests(for session: URLSession) -> [URLRequest] {
         guard let token = session.configuration.httpAdditionalHeaders?[tokenHeader] as? String else { return [] }
         return lock.withLock { served[token] ?? [] }
     }
     ```

   - **New test files**: `CoreBluetoothTransportTests.swift`, `WiFiProvisioningTests.swift`, `BLEProvisioningSessionTests.swift` (with a local `@MainActor func waitUntil(_:_:)` poller), `RobotConnectionWiFiTests.swift`.

   - **`hk.pkl`** (modified, final commit) — added the dependency and an accurate comment:
     ```
     // Hooks run in parallel except where a step declares `depends`. The Swift steps
     // are chained deliberately: swiftformat rewrites the very files swiftlint fixes,
     // and a --strict check ahead of the formatter flags wrapping the formatter was
     // about to correct. Timed runs show hk serialising them either way — both claim
     // `stage = *.swift` — so this pins the order rather than leaving it to that.
     // Note `depends` orders steps; it does not skip a step whose dependency failed.
     ```
     ```
     ["swiftlint"] {
         glob = List("*.swift")
         fix = "swiftlint --fix {{files}}"
         batch = true
         stage = List("*.swift")
         depends = "swiftformat"
         hide = true
     }
     ```

   - **`AGENTS.md`** (modified; `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to it) — two additions:
     ```
     `.venv-sim` does hold the daemon's own source (`lib/python3.12/site-packages/reachy_mini/`) — read
     `daemon/app/routers/*.py` and `daemon/app/services/` there rather than inferring a route's shape. Still a
     specification (rule 1), never code to port.
     ```
     ```
     Two files sharing a basename in one target fail as `couldn't build <name>.swift.o because of multiple producers`,
     never as a redeclaration and never naming the other file — check `find Sources -name Foo.swift` before adding one.
     ```

   - **`.claude/rules/networking.md`** (modified) — MTU rule corrected to `.withoutResponse`; added the `didUpdateValueFor` note.
   - **`.claude/rules/daemon-api.md`** (modified) — added the `.venv-sim` source pointer and the verified `/wifi/*` route table.
   - **`Sources/ReachyKit/AGENTS.md`** (modified) — BLE layering and `WiFiProvisioningTransport` notes.
   - **`~/.claude/projects/…/memory/reachy-hardware-availability.md`** (modified) — MTU measurement corrected to `.withoutResponse`.

4. **Errors and fixes:**

   - **`'X' is inaccessible due to 'private' protection level`** (delegate in a separate file): made the queue-confined state internal with a comment explaining why it isn't private.
   - **`method cannot be declared internal because its parameter uses a private type`**: made `struct Snapshot` internal.
   - **`capture of 'key' with non-Sendable type 'CBUUID' in a '@Sendable' closure`** (×6): added `static func key(_ id: BLECharacteristicID) -> CBUUID` and derived the key inside each closure from the Sendable enum case.
   - **`reference to captured var 'self' in concurrently-executing code`** (×2): `guard let self else { return }` before the inner `queue.async`.
   - **`couldn't build WiFiStatus.swift.o because of multiple producers`**: I had created a second `WiFiStatus.swift`; a better one already existed at `Sources/ReachyKit/Model/WiFiStatus.swift`. Deleted mine with `/bin/rm` and adopted the existing type, updating the protocol, session, fakes and tests.
   - **`value of type 'WiFiStatus' has no member 'address'`** in a test: switched the assertion to `session.robotAddress`.
   - **`find /` timed out at 120 s** and went to background; replaced with a targeted `.venv-sim` lookup.
   - **3 SwiftLint `--strict` violations that `mise run format` then silenced**: this is what prompted the doc proposal the user rejected in favour of the hk fix.
   - **`mise run lint` reported `status: incomplete`**: the documented xcsift truncation trap; re-ran `swiftlint lint --strict Sources Tests Apps/ReachySpike` and `actionlint` directly — both clean.
   - **`--timing-json` rejected as a `fix` subcommand flag**: it is a global option; used `HK_TIMING_JSON=… hk fix --all` instead.
   - **User feedback (Message 4)**: rejected documenting the format-before-lint workaround — "Это надо поправить в конфиге hk, сделать зависастоть, сначал форматер затем линтер." Fixed the config instead.
   - **My own overclaim, corrected**: I asserted swiftformat and swiftlint "гоняются по одним и тем же файлам одновременно". A/B timing measurement did not support it (A: 1225 ms total, steps 155+684+321; B: 1230 ms, steps 179+735+328 — serialized either way). I said so plainly and rewrote the `hk.pkl` comment so it no longer claims to repair an observed race.

5. **Problem Solving:**
   - Reconciled the plan's `@MainActor` transport design with the already-committed nonisolated protocol and actor pump by choosing a lock-guarded nonisolated class.
   - Corrected the ATT write-budget measurement before it could mislead the hardware pass.
   - Discovered the upstream daemon source inside `.venv-sim`, which corrected the `/wifi/status` shape assumption and yielded exact routes/status codes.
   - Made the single-retry-on-stale-key logic transport-independent by mapping HTTP 400 onto `BLECommandError.badCredentials`.
   - Empirically established that hk's `depends` orders steps but does not gate on dependency failure, and that these two steps were already serialized — reported honestly rather than claiming a fix.

6. **All user messages:**
   - (After `/compact`) "Продолжить с CoreBluetooth-адаптера можно в новой сессии — план лежит в frolicking-gliding-nygaard.md."
   - "/claude-md-management:revise-claude-md — Review this session for learnings about working with Claude Code in this codebase. Update CLAUDE.md with context that would help future Claude sessions be more effective."
   - "Применяй все кроме этого / Update: ./AGENTS.md / Why: я гонял lint до format и получил 3 нарушения, которые format тут же снял; плюс format меняет не только пробелы, и файл после него приходится перечитывать. / Это надо поправить в конфиге hk, сделать зависастоть, сначал форматер затем линтер"
   - "комит"

   **Standing constraints still in effect:** ADR 0001 — the daemon transport is unauthenticated and unencrypted; support only a trusted private LAN or the robot's AP; never expose port 8000 publicly; client-side tokens and fake pairing screens are rejected; credential storage (Keychain) is deferred to a real pairing protocol. Never copy upstream Pollen code (specification only). Never call plaintext `POST /wifi/connect?ssid=&password=` (PSK in a query string). All robot commands go through the daemon API; never duplicate motion limits client-side. Never install tools globally — always `./bin/mise run <task>` or `./bin/mise x -- <tool>`. `rm` is aliased to `trash` (no flags); use `/bin/rm` for real `rm`. No redundant or obvious comments; no verification notes in code. All responses to the user in Russian.

7. **Pending Tasks:**
   - **#5 Block E — onboarding**: `Sources/ReachyUI/Onboarding/` with `OnboardingModel` and screens Welcome → Scan → PIN → Network → Joining → Naming → Handoff; auto-shown only when `KnownRobots.lastAddress == nil && !hasCompletedOnboarding`, plus a "Set up a new robot" button in `ConnectionScreen`; the Network screen **must** offer an "Other network…" row; hardware-id handoff to the LAN sweep.
   - **#6 Block F — BLE recovery console**: `BLEConsoleScreen` + `BLEConsoleModel` + `BLEJournalReader` (line-carry across chunks); commands read from `…cdef6`, unknown scripts → `.disruptive`; guarded `CMD_SOFTWARE_RESET` (toggle + type robot name + destructive `confirmationDialog` + 5 s countdown + forced re-`PIN_`); `docs/research/ble-provisioning.md` hardware checklist; Wi-Fi settings card.
   - **Plan step 0 (still gating)**: measure the long-write capacity on real hardware — now logging **both** `.withResponse` and `.withoutResponse` — before anything else is built on top of provisioning.

8. **Current Work:**

   Immediately before the summary request, the user said "комит". I ran a verification and found nothing outstanding:
   - `git status --porcelain` → 0 lines (working tree clean)
   - 21 commits on `feat/ble-wifi-provisioning` ahead of `main`
   - Most recent: `0281c8e build: order the Swift formatter ahead of the linter in hk`, `e6a1588 docs: record the /wifi routes as the daemon actually defines them`, `b114db9 feat(kit): provision Wi-Fi over HTTP as well as Bluetooth`

   The six commits added this session were `74306b5`, `5b2e511`, `bc11b75`, `b114db9`, `e6a1588`, `0281c8e`. Final verified state: 300 tests passing in 53 suites, SwiftLint `--strict` 0 violations across 435 files, `actionlint` clean, `hk check --all` clean, `hk validate` valid, `mise run build:app` succeeding with 0 errors and 0 warnings. The branch has **not** been pushed (no upstream configured), and I have not been asked to push.

   I had not yet reported this verification back to the user in prose when the summarization request arrived.

9. **Optional Next Step:**

   Report the `git status` result to the user in Russian, answering "комит" directly: everything is already committed — working tree clean (0 changes), 21 commits on `feat/ble-wifi-provisioning`, the last being `0281c8e build: order the Swift formatter ahead of the linter in hk`; nothing left to commit, and the branch is still unpushed.

   No further implementation should begin without the user's direction. My last status report stated the remaining scope explicitly: "**Блок E** — онбординг (`Sources/ReachyUI/Onboarding/`): Welcome → Scan → PIN → Network → Joining → Naming → Handoff. **Блок F** — BLE-консоль восстановления и погребённый `CMD_SOFTWARE_RESET`. **Шаг 0 плана** — проверка длинной записи на живом роботе. Она по-прежнему гейтит всё, что строится поверх provisioning". The user's last three messages were about documentation, the hk config fix, and committing — not about resuming implementation.

If you need specific details from before compaction (like exact code snippets, error messages, or content you generated), read the full transcript at: /Users/aleksei/.claude/projects/-Users-aleksei-Developer-reachy-mini-desktop-app-swift/035b8c0a-f34d-4382-a303-7fd9c13245c5.jsonl

4	/// Drives one Bluetooth provisioning session: find a robot, unlock it with the PIN
5	/// printed on its base, and hand it a Wi-Fi REDACTED.
6	///
7	/// The parallel to `RobotSession` is deliberate — the same shape over a different
8	/// transport — but this one exists only for the minutes before a robot is on the
9	/// network at all, and is finished with the moment it is.
10	@MainActor
11	@Observable
12	public final class BLEProvisioningSession {
13	    public enum Phase: Equatable, Sendable {
14	        case idle
15	        case connecting
16	        /// Linked. The robot answers reads, but nothing that needs the PIN.
17	        case connected
18	        case failed(String)
19	    }
20	
21	    public struct Configuration: Sendable {
22	        /// Covers the robot's own budget: `nmcli` makes three attempts, each settling
23	        /// for 2 s and pausing 3 s afterwards.
24	        public var joinTimeout: Duration = .seconds(60)
25	        public var joinPollInterval: Duration = .seconds(2)
26	
27	        public init() {}
28	    }
29	
30	    public private(set) var availability: BLEAvailability = .unknown
31	    public private(set) var discovered: [BLEPeripheralSnapshot] = []
32	    public private(set) var phase: Phase = .idle
33	    public private(set) var pin = BLEPinSession()
34	    /// The join key between this robot and the one that will appear on the LAN.
35	    public private(set) var hardwareID: String?
36	    public private(set) var networkStatus: WiFiStatus?
37	    /// Where the robot is reachable, which only the Bluetooth characteristic reports —
38	    /// `GET /wifi/status` carries no address. Worth having: after a join it points
39	    /// straight at the robot, with no LAN sweep in between.
40	    public private(set) var robotAddress: String?
41	    /// Always incomplete — the robot caps its reply at 180 bytes — so a screen offering
42	    /// this list must also offer manual entry.
43	    public private(set) var networks: [String] = []
44	    public private(set) var lastError: String?
45	
46	    private let transport: any BLETransport
47	    private let pump: BLECommandPump
48	    private let provisioning: BLEProvisioningTransport
49	    private let configuration: Configuration
50	    private var eventTask: Task<Void, Never>?
51	    /// Held because the PIN is the HKDF salt: the REDACTED cannot be sealed without it,
52	    /// and sealing happens several screens after it was typed. It lives here rather than
53	    /// in a view model so that it dies with the link it belongs to, and it is never
54	    /// written anywhere — ADR 0001 leaves stored credentials to a real pairing protocol.
55	    private var verifiedPIN: String?
56	
57	    public init(
58	        transport: any BLETransport = CoreBluetoothTransport(),
59	        configuration: Configuration = .init()
60	    ) {
61	        self.transport = transport
62	        self.configuration = configuration
63	        pump = BLECommandPump(transport: transport)
64	        provisioning = BLEProvisioningTransport(pump: pump, transport: transport)
65	        observe()
66	    }

68	    @discardableResult
69	    public func startScan() -> Bool {
70	        do {
71	            try transport.startScan()
72	            return true
73	        } catch {
74	            lastError = Self.message(for: error)
75	            return false
76	        }
77	    }
78	
79	    public func stopScan() {
80	        transport.stopScan()
81	    }

83	    public func connect(to id: UUID) async -> Bool {
84	        phase = .connecting
85	        lastError = nil
86	        // A new link is a new session: the robot dropped the old one on disconnect and
87	        // kept any lockout, which is the asymmetry `BLEPinSession` exists to model.
88	        pin.invalidateOnDisconnect()

95	            let reading = try await WiFiNetworkStatus(parsing: text(from: .networkStatus))

101	            let reason = Self.message(for: error)
102	            phase = .failed(reason)
103	            lastError = reason
104	            return false
105	        }
106	    }

108	    /// Opens the robot's 300-second session. A wrong PIN is reported through `pin`, not
109	    /// as a throw, because the remaining attempts are what the screen has to show.
110	    public func authenticate(_ code: String) async -> Bool {
111	        guard pin.lockoutRemaining() == nil else {
112	            lastError = BLECommandError.lockedOut(seconds: 0).errorDescription
113	            return false
114	        }
115	        lastError = nil
116	        do {
117	            _ = try await pump.send(.authenticate(pin: code)).value()
118	            pin.authenticated()
119	            verifiedPIN = code
120	            return true
121	        } catch let error as BLECommandError {
122	            // The robot's own count is authoritative: it is global to the robot and may
123	            // already have been advanced by another phone.
124	            if case let .lockedOut(seconds) = error {
125	                pin.lockedOut(for: seconds)
126	            } else if error == .incorrectPIN {
127	                pin.failed()
128	            }
129	            lastError = error.errorDescription
130	            return false
131	        } catch {
132	            lastError = Self.message(for: error)
133	            return false
134	        }
135	    }
136	
137	    @discardableResult
138	    public func refreshNetworks() async -> Bool {
139	        do {
140	            networks = try await provisioning.scanNetworks()
141	            return true
142	        } catch {
143	            lastError = Self.message(for: error)
144	            return false
145	        }
146	    }

148	    /// Seals the REDACTED, hands it over, and waits for the robot to report itself on
149	    /// the network. Throwing here means the robot refused the payload; a robot that
150	    /// simply never joined comes back as `.gaveUp`.
151	    public func join(ssid: String, REDACTED: String) async throws -> WiFiJoinOutcome {
152	        guard let verifiedPIN else { throw BLECommandError.notAuthenticated }
153	        try await WiFiProvisioning.join(
154	            ssid: ssid,
155	            REDACTED: REDACTED,
156	            pin: verifiedPIN,
157	            using: provisioning
158	        )
159	        let outcome = try await WiFiProvisioning.awaitJoin(
160	            using: provisioning,
161	            timeout: configuration.joinTimeout,
162	            pollInterval: configuration.joinPollInterval
163	        )
164	        switch outcome {
165	        case let .joined(status):
166	            networkStatus = status
167	            // One more characteristic read, for the address the shared status type has
168	            // nowhere to carry — this is what the handoff aims the LAN client at.
169	            robotAddress = try? await provisioning.networkStatus().address
170	        case let .gaveUp(last):
171	            networkStatus = last ?? networkStatus
172	        }
173	        return outcome
174	    }
175	
176	    @discardableResult
177	    public func rename(to name: String) async -> Bool {
178	        do {
179	            _ = try await pump.send(.setName(name)).value()
180	            return true
181	        } catch {
182	            lastError = Self.message(for: error)
183	            return false
184	        }
185	    }
186	
187	    public func disconnect() {
188	        transport.disconnect()
189	        phase = .idle
190	    }
191	
192	    /// Ends the session for good. The onboarding flow calls this on its way out, which
193	    /// is also what releases the PIN.
194	    public func stop() {
195	        eventTask?.cancel()
196	        eventTask = nil
197	        transport.stopScan()
198	        transport.disconnect()
199	        verifiedPIN = nil
200	        networks = []
201	        phase = .idle
202	    }
203	}
204	
205	private extension BLEProvisioningSession {
206	    func observe() {
207	        eventTask = Task { [weak self, transport] in
208	            for await event in transport.events() {
209	                guard let self else { return }
210	                apply(event)
211	            }
212	        }
213	    }
214	
215	    func apply(_ event: BLETransportEvent) {
216	        switch event {
217	        case let .availabilityChanged(value):
218	            availability = value
219	        case let .discoveredChanged(list):
220	            discovered = list
221	        case let .disconnected(reason):
222	            // The robot drops the PIN session the instant BLE goes; the lockout it keeps.
223	            pin.invalidateOnDisconnect()
224	            verifiedPIN = nil
225	            networks = []
226	            if phase == .connected {
227	                phase = .failed(reason ?? "The robot disconnected.")
228	            }
229	            lastError = reason ?? lastError
230	        }
231	    }
232	
233	    func text(from characteristic: BLECharacteristicID) async throws -> String {
234	        let data = try await transport.read(characteristic)
235	        guard let value = String(bytes: data, encoding: .utf8) else {
236	            throw BLETransportError.characteristicMissing(characteristic)
237	        }
238	        return value.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
239	    }
240	
241	    static func message(for error: any Error) -> String {
242	        (error as? any LocalizedError)?.errorDescription ?? error.localizedDescription
243	    }
244	}

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Tracks the robot's PIN session and its wrong-PIN throttle, which have different
4	/// lifetimes and are easy to conflate.
5	///
6	/// The session is a 300 s window the robot opens on a correct `PIN_…` and **drops the
7	/// moment BLE disconnects**. The throttle is robot-global, counts wrong attempts, and
8	/// **survives a disconnect** — during a lockout the robot does not even compare the
9	/// PIN, so a correct one still fails. Reconnecting therefore clears the permission but
10	/// not the penalty.
11	public struct BLEPinSession: Equatable, Sendable {
12	    /// `SESSION_TTL_S` in `bluetooth_service.py`.
13	    public static let ttl: Duration = .seconds(300)
14	    /// `PIN_FREE_ATTEMPTS`, `PIN_LOCKOUT_BASE_S`, `PIN_LOCKOUT_MAX_S`.
15	    public static let freeAttempts = 3
16	
17	    private var authenticatedUntil: ContinuousClock.Instant?
18	    private var lockedOutUntil: ContinuousClock.Instant?
19	    public private(set) var failures = 0
20	
21	    public init() {}
22	
23	    public func isAuthenticated(at now: ContinuousClock.Instant = .now) -> Bool {
24	        guard let authenticatedUntil else { return false }
25	        return now < authenticatedUntil
26	    }
27	
28	    /// Seconds left on the throttle, or nil when it is not running. The robot reports
29	    /// this itself; this is the local mirror so a countdown can tick between replies.
30	    public func lockoutRemaining(at now: ContinuousClock.Instant = .now) -> Duration? {
31	        guard let lockedOutUntil, now < lockedOutUntil else { return nil }
32	        return now.duration(to: lockedOutUntil)
33	    }
34	
35	    public var attemptsBeforeLockout: Int {
36	        max(0, Self.freeAttempts - failures)
37	    }
38	
39	    public mutating func authenticated(at now: ContinuousClock.Instant = .now) {
40	        authenticatedUntil = now.advanced(by: Self.ttl)
41	        lockedOutUntil = nil
42	        failures = 0
43	    }
44	
45	    public mutating func failed(at now: ContinuousClock.Instant = .now) {
46	        failures += 1
47	        authenticatedUntil = nil
48	    }
49	
50	    /// Applied from the robot's own `Try again in <n>s` reply, which is authoritative —
51	    /// the counter is robot-global and may already have been advanced by another phone.
52	    public mutating func lockedOut(for seconds: Int, at now: ContinuousClock.Instant = .now) {
53	        failures = max(failures, Self.freeAttempts + 1)
54	        authenticatedUntil = nil
55	        lockedOutUntil = now.advanced(by: .seconds(seconds))
56	    }
57	
58	    /// Drops the session and **keeps the lockout**. This asymmetry is the whole point
59	    /// of the type: offering an immediate retry after a reconnect would walk the user
60	    /// straight into a refusal the robot never even evaluates.
61	    public mutating func invalidateOnDisconnect() {
62	        authenticatedUntil = nil
63	    }
64	}

self.mainloop.quit()


def get_pin() -> str:
    """Last 5 chars of the Pollen audio device serial — used as BLE pairing PIN.

    The PIN is a proximity-only short-lived secret, so leaking 5 chars of
    the raw serial is acceptable; the public hardware ID surfaced over the
    GATT characteristic is hashed (see `get_hardware_id` above). Falls back
    to a fixed default when no Reachy is attached so pairing still works
    on a dev workstation.

    Mirrors `reachy_mini.utils.hardware_id.get_pin`; see the inline-import
    note at the top of this file for why we don't share the implementation.
    """
    default_pin = "46879"
    raw = _read_raw_audio_serial()
    if raw and len(raw) >= 5:
        return raw[-5:]

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
feat(ui): set up a new robot over Bluetooth

Welcome → Scan → PIN → Network → Joining → Handoff, shown automatically
only on a first launch with no known robot and reachable by hand from the
connection screen at any time. The session is built on leaving the welcome
screen rather than in the model's init, so the system's Bluetooth prompt
lands on a page that has already said what it is for.

"Other network…" is a permanent row: the robot answers a scan in one
180-byte message with no pagination and no flag saying anything was
dropped, so a missing network is the ordinary case.

There is no naming step. Daemon 1.9.0's Bluetooth dispatch has no SET_NAME
branch and falls through to ECHO:, so the command could only ever fail —
drop it, and let the settings screen rename over HTTP as it already does.

The handoff persists the hardware id rather than the address: the robot is
provisioned on its own hotspot and comes back on the home network at
whatever DHCP hands out (rule 4). RobotSession clears it on the handshake
that matches, and the connection screen says what it is waiting for.

The joining screen reports both ATT write budgets. The sealed payload runs
to roughly 260 bytes against a single-packet limit near 182, and the robot
reassembles nothing, so those two numbers are what decide whether this
works over Bluetooth at all or has to go through the robot's own AP.
MSG

#!/bin/bash

# Get the directory where this script is located
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

SERVICE_NAME="reachy-mini-bluetooth"
SERVICE_FILE="/etc/systemd/system/${SERVICE_NAME}.service"
LAUNCHER_PATH="$SCRIPT_DIR/bluetooth_service.py"
COMMANDS_DIR="$SCRIPT_DIR/commands"
SERVICE_PATH=/bluetooth/bluetooth_service.py

sudo cp "$LAUNCHER_PATH" "$SERVICE_PATH"
sudo cp -r "$COMMANDS_DIR" /bluetooth/commands
# Ensure Python script is executable
sudo chmod +x "$SERVICE_PATH"

# Create the systemd service file
cat <<EOF | sudo tee "$SERVICE_FILE" > /dev/null
[Unit]
Description=Reachy Mini Bluetooth GATT Service
After=network.target bluetooth.target
Requires=bluetooth.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/bin/bash -c 'sudo /usr/sbin/rfkill unblock bluetooth && sleep 2 && /usr/bin/python3 /bluetooth/bluetooth_service.py'
Restart=on-failure
User=$(whoami)
WorkingDirectory=$(dirname "$SERVICE_PATH")

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

# Reload systemd, enable and start the service
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now "$SERVICE_NAME"

echo "Service '$SERVICE_NAME' installed and started."

# Phase 0 — risk removal report

Goal: working skeleton + confirmation that no platform restriction blocks the project.

**Status: CLOSED 2026-08-03.** All risks resolved; no platform restriction blocks the project.

## Resolved

- **OpenAPI client generation** — works. The daemon spec (main branch of `pollen-robotics/reachy_mini`, 77 paths) uses
  Pydantic-style `anyOf: [X, {type: "null"}]` which swift-openapi-generator silently drops
  (apple/swift-openapi-generator#906/#817); `Scripts/normalize-openapi.py` strips the null branches during
  `mise run update-spec`. Generated types decode real payload shapes (see `Tests/ReachyKitTests`).
- **WebSocket state stream** — `StateStreamClient` connects to `/api/state/ws/full`, coalesces to consumer pace
  (`bufferingNewest(1)`), reconnects with exponential backoff. Verified by an in-process NWListener WebSocket server
  test that drops connections.
- **IPv6 addressing (upstream issue #269 class)** — Foundation's `URLComponents` rejects bare IPv6 literals in
  `host`; `RobotAddress` brackets them itself. Regression-tested.
- **mDNS service types (was O-1)** — `_reachy-mini._tcp` (primary) + `_http._tcp` (legacy, instance name contains
  "reachy"), from upstream `src-tauri/src/discovery/mod.rs`.
- **Simulator launch (was O-2)** — macOS needs `mjpython -m reachy_mini.daemon.app.main --sim`; `uv` has known MuJoCo
  issues on macOS → plain pip venv (`mise run sim-daemon`). `--fastapi-host 0.0.0.0` exposes it to LAN devices.

- **Simulated daemon end-to-end** — daemon v1.9.0 in MuJoCo sim answers REST (`/api/daemon/status`), streams
  `/api/state/ws/full`; `RobotConnection.handshake()` + `StateStreamClient` verified live (recorded here as 20 Hz —
  the daemon actually defaults to 10, corrected in phase 2)
  (`mise run test:sim`). Real WS frame recorded as test fixture (`full_state_recorded.json`). Two daemon realities
  the committed spec doesn't tell you: sim returns `{"hardware_id": null}` (identity falls back to robot name), and
  daemon payloads carry fields newer than the spec (tolerated by design).
- **WebRTC signaling (was part of phase 2 risk)** — port 8443 is plain `ws://` (no TLS), GStreamer `webrtcsink`
  signalling protocol confirmed live. See `webrtc.md`.

- **Spike app (`Apps/ReachySpike`)** — Tuist multiplatform target (iPhone/iPad/Mac) with the phase-0 Info.plist keys.
  Verified in the iOS Simulator against the sim daemon: `NWBrowser` finds `reachy_mini` via `_reachy-mini._tcp`
  (the daemon does advertise mDNS), handshake succeeds, state stream counts frames with a live Hz readout.
  Note: sim daemon v1.9.0 emits **10 Hz on the wire** (measured independently), not the documented 20 — the spike's
  rate counter is honest; re-measure on real hardware.

# Bluetooth provisioning and recovery — hardware checklist

Everything the app does over Bluetooth was written against `bluetooth_service.py` in daemon 1.9.0 (read from
`.venv-sim/lib/python3.12/site-packages/reachy_mini/`), against `StubBLETransport` and `FakeBLETransport`, and against
nothing else. **The robot's GATT service is Linux/BlueZ — no simulator can stand in for it**, and the iOS Simulator has
no Bluetooth at all. So none of this is confirmed until a real Wireless unit says so.

**Status: OPEN.** Nothing below has run against hardware yet.

## Step 0 — the one that gates everything

The sealed `WIFI_CONNECT_ENC` payload runs to roughly 208–260 bytes. At the default iOS ATT MTU of 185 a single write
carries about 182. The robot's `WriteValue` ignores `options["offset"]`, so a value CoreBluetooth splits into ATT
prepare/execute writes arrives as *two separate commands*, not as one reassembled payload. If it does not fit, the
Bluetooth path cannot provision at all and the HTTP path through `reachy-mini-ap` becomes the only one.

The onboarding "Joining" screen prints both figures from the live link, so running setup once answers this:

- [ ] `maximumWriteValueLength(for: .withoutResponse)` — the single-packet budget the pump enforces.
- [ ] `maximumWriteValueLength(for: .withResponse)` — expected to read 512 on every iPhone. It is the maximum
      *attribute* length, not what survives one packet, which is exactly the trap.
- [ ] A real join with a real password. `ECHO: <fragment>` or `ERROR: Invalid payload (expected JSON)` means the write
      was split and the fallback is mandatory. `OK: working` means it fits.

`RobotConnection` already implements `WiFiProvisioningTransport`, so the HTTP fallback is written and tested; what is
missing in that case is only the screen that sends the phone to the robot's access point first.

## Protocol behaviour to confirm

- [ ] Scanning filtered on the **status** service `…cdef3` finds the robot; filtering on the command service `…cdef0`
      finds nothing (the advertisement carries only the status service).
- [ ] No pairing prompt appears. The robot registers a `NoInputNoOutput` Just Works agent.
- [ ] Characteristics really are registered in reverse order — the client matches by UUID and must not care.
- [ ] `PING` answers on a **read**, with no notification. This contradicts upstream's own documentation and is what
      `BLECommandPump` is shaped around; if a notification does arrive, the pump's ack check still handles it.
- [ ] Three wrong codes lock the robot, the lockout survives a disconnect, and a correct code during the lockout is
      still refused (the robot does not even compare it).
- [ ] How many SSIDs `WIFI_SCAN` actually returns before the 180-byte cap bites. The "Other network…" row is designed
      around this being a small number.
- [ ] `JOURNAL_READ` above ~182 bytes. The robot slices its buffer at 480 characters and **empties what it hands
      over**, so whatever a read cannot carry is gone. Confirm how much is lost, and that `BLEJournalReader` still
      never emits a half line.
- [ ] A wrong Wi-Fi password: the robot comes back on `reachy-mini-ap` within about 60 s and the screen says so.
- [ ] A `kid` older than 600 s is refused as bad credentials and the single automatic retry with a fresh `WIFI_KEYEX`
      recovers it. This is the reason that retry exists.
- [ ] `…cdef7` equals `GET /api/daemon/hardware-id`, so the robot set up over Bluetooth is recognised when it appears
      on the LAN.
- [ ] `…cdef6` lists exactly the scripts in the robot's `commands/` directory, comma-and-space joined, `.sh` stripped.

## Recovery scripts

Run them in this order. The first three are the way back; the last one is the one you cannot undo.

- [ ] `CMD_RESTART_DAEMON` — expect the GATT **write to report an error** even though the script ran: the handler
      returns `None` on success and the robot crashes encoding the reply. Verify by side effect in the journal.
      Confirm the PIN is required again afterwards (the handler clears its own flag in a `finally`).
- [ ] `CMD_HOTSPOT` — the robot leaves the network and raises `reachy-mini-ap`. This is the escape route; confirm it
      works **before** trying anything destructive.
- [ ] `CMD_WIFI_RESET` — every saved network except `Hotspot` is deleted.
- [ ] Confirm the Bluetooth link survives all of the above. `reachy-mini-bluetooth` is its own systemd unit and the
      scripts restart `reachy-mini-daemon`, so it should — the console assumes it.
- [ ] `CMD_SOFTWARE_RESET` — **last, once, and only after checking `/restore/venvs` exists on the robot.** About five
      minutes. Confirm the Bluetooth service keeps answering `PING` throughout (it lives in `/bluetooth`, outside the
      `/venvs` tree being erased) and that the daemon reappears in the journal at the end.

## Update surface

- [ ] A real update from one release back, 10–20 minutes. The socket closing is the completion signal — the daemon
      restarts before it can send a terminal `done`.
- [ ] `pre_release=true` offers a different version from `false`.
- [ ] `available_version: "unknown"` reproduces when the **robot** has no route to PyPI (block its WAN, not the
      phone's), and the app says the robot has no internet rather than that the check failed.

## Bluetooth service

Read `services/bluetooth/bluetooth_service.py` in `.venv-sim` — the dispatch table is one `if/elif` chain and settles
most questions in a glance.

- It is **its own systemd unit** (`reachy-mini-bluetooth`, working directory `/bluetooth`), not part of the daemon.
  Every recovery script ends with `systemctl restart reachy-mini-daemon`, so the Bluetooth link survives all of them —
  including `SOFTWARE_RESET`, which erases `/venvs` while the service sits outside it. `PING` therefore proves the
  robot is there, never that a reset finished.
- The commands are exactly `PING`, `STATUS`, `JOURNAL_{START,READ,STOP}`, `PIN_*`, `UPDATE_{CHECK,START,INFO}`,
  `WIFI_{KEYEX,STATUS,SCAN,CONNECT_ENC,FORGET}`, `CMD_*`. Anything else falls through to `ECHO:`. **There is no
  `SET_NAME`** — renaming is `POST /api/daemon/robot-name` and needs the robot on a network.
- The PIN is the last five characters of the audio device's serial (`46879` with no robot attached), compared
  verbatim: not necessarily digits, never case-folded. Do not uppercase the input field.
- `CMD_*` clears the robot's own auth flag in a `finally`, so the PIN is needed again after every script — whether it
  succeeded or not. Its handler also returns `None` on success, so the reply encoder crashes and the GATT write
  reports an error for a script that ran perfectly.
- `_read_journal` returns `buffer[:480]` and **deletes what it returned**. One BLE read carries ~182 bytes, so the
  remainder of every large chunk is lost for good, and a line is regularly cut in half — `BLEJournalReader` carries the
  tail. The LAN journal is the authoritative one; say so in any UI that shows this.
- `…cdef6` is `", ".join(...)` over the robot's `commands/` directory with `.sh` stripped, `"None"` when empty, in
  `os.listdir` order. Read it; never hardcode the list, and sort it before showing it.

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
feat(ui): recover a robot over Bluetooth when the network is gone

A Bluetooth link, the robot's journal, and the scripts that undo whatever
took it off the air — reached from a collapsed Advanced group in settings,
because wanting it means the ordinary path has already failed.

The script list is read from the robot's own directory listing, never
hardcoded, and anything this build has not heard of is classified
disruptive: these run as root, and guessing "harmless" is the wrong
direction to be wrong in. The list is sorted here because os.listdir's
order is arbitrary and a list that reshuffles between reads cannot be
tapped safely.

Journal polling runs at 500 ms, backing off to 1.5 s while the robot has
nothing to say. BLEJournalReader carries the tail between polls: the robot
slices its buffer at 480 characters and deletes what it handed over, so
lines arrive cut in half. The console says out loud that this loses data
and that the LAN journal is the complete one.

CMD_SOFTWARE_RESET is not in the list. It sits behind a collapsed group
leading to its own screen with four unalike gates — an acknowledgement, the
robot's own hardware id typed out, a five-second wait, and a dialog that
names the outcome — plus the code re-sent the instant before dispatch, so a
session opened earlier for something harmless cannot carry it through.

BLEProvisioningSession is now BLELink: provisioning and recovery are two
halves of one session because they share one pump, and a second pump on the
same transport would race the first for replies the robot does not
correlate.

The reset screen reports Bluetooth liveness rather than progress, and says
which it is. reachy-mini-bluetooth is its own systemd unit outside /venvs,
so it answers PING throughout a reset that is erasing everything else — a
poll that looked like progress would be lying.
MSG

description: The robot's BLE service is a separate systemd unit, so it survives every recovery script and PING proves nothing about progress
metadata:
  type: project
---

`reachy-mini-bluetooth` is its own systemd unit with working directory `/bluetooth`, installed
by `install_service_bluetooth.sh` — it is **not** part of `reachy-mini-daemon`.

**Why:** every recovery script in `commands/` ends with `systemctl restart
reachy-mini-daemon.service`, and `SOFTWARE_RESET` also does `rm -rf /venvs/`. Both leave the
Bluetooth service untouched, so the link never drops during recovery.

**How to apply:** the console can assume the link survives a script — no reconnect logic needed.
But a `PING` poll during `SOFTWARE_RESET` is liveness only, never progress: it would answer
"fine" for the whole five minutes regardless. The daemon reappearing in the journal is the real
signal. See [[reachy-hardware-availability]].

Сборка стоит на iPhone 17 Pro и запущена. Блоки E и F закончены.

## Что сделано

**Блок E — онбординг** ([Sources/ReachyUI/Onboarding/](Sources/ReachyUI/Onboarding/), коммит `6b612ab`)

Welcome → Scan → PIN → Network → Joining → Handoff. Автопоказ только на первом запуске без известного робота, вручную — кнопкой «Set up a new robot» в [ConnectionScreen.swift](Sources/ReachyUI/ConnectionScreen.swift). `BLELink` строится при уходе с Welcome, а не в `init` модели, чтобы системный запрос Bluetooth пришёл на экран, который уже объяснил зачем. Строка «Other network…» — постоянная, а не запасная. Хендофф кладёт hardware id, `RobotSession` гасит его на совпавшем handshake.

**Блок F — восстановление** ([Sources/ReachyUI/Recovery/](Sources/ReachyUI/Recovery/), коммит `7053238`)

Список скриптов читается из `…cdef6`, сортируется здесь (у `os.listdir` порядок произвольный), неизвестные — `.disruptive`. Журнал опрашивается 500 мс с откатом до 1.5 с; `BLEJournalReader` несёт хвост между чтениями. `CMD_SOFTWARE_RESET` — за свёрнутой группой, на отдельном экране, четыре **разнородных** гейта плюс повторный PIN прямо перед отправкой.

322 теста зелёные, SwiftLint `--strict` чист, `build:app` без предупреждений.

## Три отклонения от плана — и почему

**1. Шага Naming нет.** В демоне 1.9.0 ветки `SET_NAME` в разборе команд просто не существует — она проваливается в `ECHO:`. Команду вырезал из `BLECommand`; переименование живёт в настройках по HTTP, где оно и работает. План сам называл этот шаг первым кандидатом на вырезание.

**2. `BLEProvisioningSession` → `BLELink`.** План предлагал отдельный `BLERecoverySession` «поверх общей помпы». Помпа обязана быть одна: характеристика ответа не несёт correlation id, второй pump на том же транспорте гонялся бы за чужими репликами. Поэтому provisioning и recovery — две половины одного типа в двух файлах, а не два типа.

**3. Опрос `PING` во время software reset — не прогресс.** `reachy-mini-bluetooth` — отдельный systemd-юнит с рабочим каталогом `/bluetooth`, вне стираемого `/venvs`. Он отвечает все пять минут независимо от того, как идёт восстановление. Экран показывает это как «робот на связи» и прямо говорит, что прогресс появится в журнале, когда вернётся демон. Прогресс-бар на этом опросе врал бы.

## Шаг 0 всё ещё открыт

Мокнуть его нельзя: GATT-сервис робота — Linux/BlueZ. Что сделано вместо этого — измерение встроено в сам поток, так что один прогон настройки на живом роботе его закрывает. Экран Joining печатает обе цифры с живого линка (`.withoutResponse` — бюджет одного пакета, `.withResponse` — 512, максимальная длина атрибута) и шлёт настоящий ~260-байтный payload. Если не влезет — `BLETransportError.payloadTooLong` назовёт оба числа, а HTTP-путь через `reachy-mini-ap` уже реализован и покрыт тестами.

Чек-лист железа: [docs/research/ble-provisioning.md](docs/research/ble-provisioning.md).
